title: Geometric-point product sheaves: adjunction, exactness and evaluation acyclicity
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $R$ a commutative ring, and $P$ any small indexed family of geometric points of $X$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use ordinary small-etale $R_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and nonnegative injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a family of $R$-modules $M=(M_p)_{p\in P}$ define the presheaf
$$B_P(M)(V)=\prod_{p\in P}\prod_{v:p\to V}M_p$$
on etale $V\to X$, with restriction by precomposition on the lift index and maps induced coordinatewise. This presheaf is a sheaf. The functor $B_P$ is right adjoint to the exact functor $A_P:F\mapsto(F_p)_{p\in P}$, with unit the tuple of germ maps. For every etale $V\to X$, the functor $M\mapsto B_P(M)(V)$ is exact; in particular $B_P$ is exact. If each $M_p$ is injective as an $R$-module, $B_P(M)$ is an injective $R_X$-module sheaf. Every family $M$ admits a family of nonnegative injective module resolutions $M_p\to J_p^\bullet$, and applying $B_P$ degreewise gives an injective sheaf resolution $B_P(M)\to B_P(J^\bullet)$. For every etale $V\to X$ and integer $a>0$,
$$R^a\Gamma(V,-)(B_P(M))=0,$$
where $\Gamma(V,-)$ is evaluation on $V$ and its right derived functors are taken in the category of $R_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No conservativity of $P$, finiteness of $R$ or $M_p$, or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 04EQ (lemma-stalk-exact-modules), 05V8 (lemma-skyscraper-modules-exact); point adjunction and product formula: sites.tex Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf). Injective resolutions: injectives.tex Tag 01DU (theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives), applied also to the one-point ringed site. The product-family and evaluation-acyclic formulation is agent-explicit.

proof.text: Write $L_p(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(p,V)$. By [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point], the presheaf $V\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(L_p(V),M_p)$ is a sheaf of sets. The product over $p$ is a sheaf: glue a matching family separately at each $p$, and uniqueness at each coordinate gives uniqueness of the product gluing. Addition and the constant $R$-action are coordinatewise. To specify the full $R_X(V)$-action, send $a\in R_X(V)$ to its germ $a_{p,v}\in R$ at each $(p,v)$ and put $(a m)_{p,v}=a_{p,v}m_{p,v}$. The identification $(R_X)_p=R$ is [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] applied to the additive group of $R$; it respects multiplication and $1$, since the germ and constant-section maps respect those operations. Germs commute with restriction, so this action makes the product an $R_X$-module sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Precomposition on lift indices and coordinatewise maps in $M$ preserve all these operations and define $B_P$.

source.place: Tag 00Y8, lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf (1); module action as in sites-modules.tex, Section 04EM (section-stalks), and etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) (2)

proof.text: For $R$-linear maps $t_p:F_p\to M_p$, define $h_V(s)_{p,v}=t_p([V,v,s])$. This commutes with restriction by the definition of germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and is $R_X(V)$-linear because $[V,v,a s]=a_{p,v}[V,v,s]$. Conversely, a module-sheaf map $h:F\to B_P(M)$ gives $t_p([V,v,s])=h_V(s)_{p,v}$. It is well-defined: the opposite pointed-neighbourhood category is filtered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so equal germs agree on a common refinement, and naturality of $h$ gives equal coordinates there. The same refinement checks addition; constant sections check $R$-linearity. The two constructions are inverse, as is seen on every representative $[V,v,s]$ and every coordinate $(p,v)$. Both commute with maps in $F$ and in $M$, giving the adjunction $A_P\dashv B_P$. Taking all $t_p$ to be identities gives exactly the tuple of germ maps as its unit.

source.place: Tag 00Y7, lemma-adjoint-point-push-stalk, proof; Tag 00Y8, lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf (2); the formula is written explicitly for modules and a family of points

proof.text: The forgetful functor from $R_X$-module sheaves to abelian sheaves is faithful and exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Thus a short exact sequence of module sheaves gives a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves. Each geometric stalk is exact on abelian sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]; its maps here are $R$-linear. Exactness of $R$-modules is exactness of the underlying groups (the usual kernels and images in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]). Consequently each module-stalk functor is exact. Kernels and cokernels in the family category are componentwise, by their universal properties; hence $A_P$ is exact. No point-detection assertion is used.

source.place: Tags 03DA, lemma-abelian, and 04EQ, lemma-stalk-exact-modules (1); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT, lemma-stalk-exact (3)

proof.text: Fix $V\to X$. On a componentwise short exact sequence of module families the displayed formula for $B_P(-)(V)$ is exact: an element in the kernel is precisely a tuple of elements in the coordinate kernels; injectivity is checked coordinatewise; and a tuple in the final product lifts by choosing a preimage separately for every $(p,v)$. These are choices over a set by [def-weil-size-convention]. Thus evaluation of $B_P$ on every $V$ is exact. The resulting sequence of sheaves is exact as well: its sectionwise kernel is its first term, and its last arrow is sectionwise surjective, so its sectionwise cokernel is zero and remains zero after sheafification. These descriptions of kernels and cokernels in the module-sheaf category are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Therefore $B_P$ is exact. Empty products are zero modules and satisfy the same assertions.

source.place: Tag 05V8, lemma-skyscraper-modules-exact (1), with the product calculation written out; kernels and cokernels: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian

proof.text: Suppose each $M_p$ is injective. Let $i:F\hookrightarrow G$ be a monomorphism of module sheaves and $h:F\to B_P(M)$. Under step 2, $h$ is a tuple $t_p:F_p\to M_p$. By step 3 each $i_p:F_p\hookrightarrow G_p$ is injective. The extension property in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] gives $\widetilde t_p:G_p\to M_p$ extending $t_p$, and small choice gives a tuple of these extensions. Its adjoint $\widetilde h:G\to B_P(M)$ satisfies $\widetilde h i=h$, because that equality holds at each adjoint component. This is the defining injectivity of $B_P(M)$.

source.place: Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives, extension-property argument, written here directly for the family adjunction

proof.text: The category of $R$-modules is abelian with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] to choose a nonnegative injective resolution $M_p\to J_p^\bullet$ for every $p$. The family is small, so these choices are simultaneous in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Its augmented complex is exact componentwise. Step 4 carries that exact augmented complex to $B_P(M)\to B_P(J^\bullet)$: equivalently, apply its kernel-image calculation at every degree. Every $B_P(J^n)$ is injective by step 5, and the complex is zero in negative degrees. This is the required injective sheaf resolution.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (1), with modules having enough injectives by more-algebra.tex Tag 01DD, lemma-injectives-modules

proof.text: The module-sheaf category has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Evaluation $\Gamma_V$ is additive, and [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], clause (2), computes its right derived functor on the bounded-below injective resolution of step 6. Since its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, $R\Gamma_V(B_P(M)[0])$ is represented by $B_P(J^\bullet)(V)$. Its differentials are the coordinate differentials of $\prod_{p,v}J_p^\bullet$. For $a>0$, a cocycle is a tuple $z_{p,v}\in\ker(d_p^a)$. Exactness of each module resolution gives $y_{p,v}\in J_p^{a-1}$ with $d_p^{a-1}y_{p,v}=z_{p,v}$. Small choice makes these into an element of $B_P(J^{a-1})(V)$ whose differential is the given cocycle. Thus $H^a(B_P(J^\bullet)(V))=0$, which is precisely $R^a\Gamma(V,-)(B_P(M))=0$. This calculation remains valid for empty lift sets and for $P=\varnothing$, and nowhere uses conservativity, Noetherianity, finiteness, or a torsion hypothesis.

split_report.summary: Split into seven explicit steps, using only existing nodes. Constructed the constant-ring-sheaf action, family adjunction and germ unit; reduced module-stalk exactness to the stated abelian-stalk theorem through the exact forgetful functor; proved sectionwise product exactness by coordinate lifts; proved injectivity by the extension property; used ordinary nonnegative module resolutions and bounded-below derived evaluation. No new nodes, statement changes, Lean edits or compiles. Retained prior genuine searches and reused the interrupted-turn search log.
split_report.blueprint: The item realizes the geometric-point-product building block in the from.place chain of lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve: the supported Godement construction required by the regular finite-coefficient purity model. Steps 1-3 establish its sheaf/stalk interface; steps 4-7 supply exact point products and evaluation acyclicity before the germ-unit resolution is iterated. Whole-blueprint searches for skyscraper, point pushforward, product sheaves and geometric stalk found no duplicate theorem. No unit or chapter route changes.
